title: slaude agent.yaml

name.description: The agent's name. Must equal the name of the directory the file sits in (personas/<name>/agent.yaml). Required. Example: ana

description.description: One or two lines on what the agent is for; it becomes the agent's role. At most 2000 characters. Example: Handles support questions for the platform team.

model.description: Model the agent runs on, provider-qualified. Leave out for the deployment default. Example: provider/model-name

slackUserId.description: The agent's own Slack user, as a user reference. Write slack:user:U0EXAMPLE; a bare Slack user id is accepted for one more release with a warning. Example: slack:user:U0EXAMPLE

userToken.description: Slack user token to post as the agent's own user, as a placeholder that CI fills in, never the token itself. Example: ${PERSONA_ANA_XOXP}

provider.description: Provider credentials and endpoint for this agent (apiKey, baseUrl, and so on). Give credentials as references such as env://PERSONA_ANA_KEY, never as values.

runsOn.description: Label of the machines this agent runs on. Leave out to run anywhere. Example: finance

soul.description: Who the agent is and how it sounds: identity, voice, values. Plain prose in a block (soul: |). Required. Mandates and access go in their own keys, not here.

global.description: What the agent is responsible for everywhere. Example: Answer support questions and keep the runbook current.

boundary.description: Where this sub-mandate applies: a channel reference such as slack:channel:C0EXAMPLE for one channel, trust:public or trust:trusted for every channel of that class, or dm for direct messages. Each boundary may appear once. The older channel:<id> is accepted for one more release with a warning; write slack:channel:<id>. Example: slack:channel:C0EXAMPLE

mode.description: How the text combines with the global mandate: override (replace it, the default), extend (add to it) or reduce (restrict it). Matching ignores case and surrounding spaces. A value that is none of these is accepted with a warning and read as extend, so a typo keeps the global mandate instead of replacing it. Example: extend

text.description: The sub-mandate itself, in the agent's own voice of duty. An extend or reduce is carried whole, so keep it under 600 characters. Example: Also watch the deploy queue.

scoped.description: Different duties for one channel, a trust class or direct messages. The most specific match applies.

mandate.description: What the agent is asked to do, globally and per place.

manager.description: The person who manages this agent and can approve for it, as a user reference. Write slack:user:U0EXAMPLE; a bare Slack user id is accepted for one more release with a warning. Example: slack:user:U0EXAMPLE

backupManager.description: Who covers when the manager is away, as a user reference. Write slack:user:U0EXAMPLE; a bare Slack user id is accepted for one more release with a warning. Example: slack:user:U0EXAMPLE

user.description: The approver, as a user reference such as slack:user:U0EXAMPLE. A bare Slack user id is accepted for one more release with a warning. Required. Example: slack:user:U0EXAMPLE

scope.description: What this person may approve, in plain words. Leave it out for an approver of anything (a catch-all). Example: budget changes

catchall.description: true if this person is asked when no other approver's scope fits. Defaults to true when scope is left out, false otherwise.

channel.description: Make this person an approver for one channel only, as a channel reference such as slack:channel:C0EXAMPLE (a bare Slack channel id is accepted for one more release with a warning). Leave it out for an approver everywhere. Example: slack:channel:C0EXAMPLE

approvers.description: People who may approve what the agent asks to do, each for a scope of work and optionally one channel.

public.description: Channels where the agent may speak with anyone present, as channel references. Write slack:channel:C0EXAMPLE; bare Slack channel ids are accepted for one more release with a warning. Example: [slack:channel:C0EXAMPLE]

trusted.description: Channels whose members the agent trusts with more, such as the team's own channel, as channel references. Write slack:channel:C0EXAMPLE; bare Slack channel ids are accepted for one more release with a warning. Example: [slack:channel:C0EXAMPLE]

channels.description: Which channels the agent works in, by trust class.

dm.description: Users the agent answers in direct messages, as user references. Write slack:user:U0EXAMPLE; bare Slack user ids are accepted for one more release with a warning. Example: [slack:user:U0EXAMPLE]

blocked.description: Users the agent ignores everywhere, as user references. Write slack:user:U0EXAMPLE; bare Slack user ids are accepted for one more release with a warning. Example: [slack:user:U0EXAMPLE]

redact.description: Patterns (JavaScript regular expressions, matched case-insensitively) whose matches are masked before the agent's text reaches Slack. Example: ["project-[a-z]+"]

approvalTimeoutSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for an approval before denying. 0 or unset uses the default. Example: 120

access.description: Who manages the agent, who approves for it, and where and with whom it works.

mcp.description: External tool servers, in the same shape as a .mcp.json file: mcpServers: { <name>: { type, url, headers } }. Give secrets as ${PERSONA_*} placeholders.

skills.description: Skills this agent may use, by name. Leave the key out for every installed skill; write [] for none. A bare `skills:` is refused. Example: [release-notes, triage]

guardrails.description: Owner guardrails that apply to this agent, by name, in addition to the shared ones. Example: [no-outbound-email]

kbSources.description: Knowledge bases the agent reads. Leave the key out for the default; write [] for none. A bare `kbSources:` is refused. Example: [kb-handbook]

background.description: Settings for background learning passes, such as budgetUsd and timezone. Example: { budgetUsd: 2, timezone: UTC }

enabled.description: true turns on the summarising round and lets its posts reach the manager and people who opted in. It starts no wake: waking is per channel (channels.<ref>.proactive). Leave the key out for off.

read.description: Further channels the agent may read with read_channel, in any turn. Example: [slack:channel:C0EXAMPLE]

watch.description: External sources the summarising round reads, by name. Example: [mail, tracker]

quietHours.description: Hours when the round does not post, local time, as HH:MM-HH:MM. A window that ends before it starts wraps midnight. Example: 21:00-08:00

maxPerDay.description: Most proactive posts to one person per day. Example: 6

proactive.description: What is not about one channel: further channels to read, sources to watch, quiet hours and the post cap. Waking is set per channel under channels.

session.description: Set to "channel" to keep one long-lived session for this channel instead of one per thread. The only value there is; leave the key out for the default. Example: channel

proactive.description: true lets the agent wake in this channel on its own and speak up; false keeps it silent here. Setting it implies a channel session. Leave the key out to change nothing.

channels.description: Per-channel behaviour, keyed by channel reference. Write slack:channel:C0EXAMPLE; a bare Slack channel id key is accepted for one more release with a warning. Example: { "slack:channel:C0EXAMPLE": { session: channel, proactive: true } }

description: A slaude agent: one file per persona, at personas/<name>/agent.yaml. Unknown keys are refused at every level.
